_notes: The provincial's desk (friar round, Q3). E3 §3.1 obedience, §3.7 the province, §3.14 closures. Every act is data; the numbers are invented. An act's target says what the sheet asks him to name: a man and a house, a house, a house under its floor, a house with something to sell, or nothing.

acts.label: Send a man
acts.blurb: A friar of the province to another of its houses, by letter, with a month's notice. He goes; the house he leaves is a man short and the one he reaches a man up.
acts.line: The letter went out on Monday. {man} will be at {house} by the first of the month, and the men at table where he was have opinions.

acts.label: Visit a house
acts.blurb: Three days in the house: the books, the chapter, every man alone for a quarter of an hour. The house tidies its observance for the week you are in it, and remembers that you came.

acts.label: Close a house
acts.blurb: A house under the floor for its kind is closed: its men go where there is room, a parish it held goes back to the diocese, and the town notices. The council has wanted this for a decade and no provincial has said it.
acts.line: {closing} The province is lighter by a house and the men who lived in it will not forget whose signature was on the letter.

acts.label: Levy the houses
acts.blurb: A tenth of every house's purse to the province, once a year. The priors write back; the procurators sigh.
acts.line: The levy brought ${amount} to the province, and a letter from every prior.

acts.label: Write to the general
acts.blurb: A subsidy from the order's curia, which reads the province's books before it answers, and remembers having been asked.

acts.label: Sell a building
acts.blurb: A house with a wing it no longer fills sells it. The province gets most of what it cost; the house gets a smaller cloister and a grievance.
acts.line: {house} sold its {building} for ${amount}. The men who had rooms in it are in rooms elsewhere.
